sources.ref_file_title: GL89 - A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions
sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki; bibliographic fields not re-verified.

pages.class_justification: Left `unstated`. The hypothesis is a concrete hardness assumption, not a primitive quantified over implementations, so the RTV04 notions (which quantify over f in F_Q) are degenerate here; every other assumption-hypothesis edge in content/Reductions is likewise unstated, while all seven fully-black-box pages have primitive hypotheses. The security reduction is nonetheless black-box in the adversary. Here the hard-core-bit reduction of ACGS88/GL89 runs any IND-CPA distinguisher as an oracle and the construction touches the RSA function only through evaluation and trapdoor inversion, so a reader who accepts assumptions as primitives would read it as fully-black-box.
pages.model_justification: No idealized oracle: the hard-core-bit construction and its reduction are standard-model.
pages.statement: The [[rsa-assumption|RSA assumption]] implies [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]. [[RSA78 - A method for obtaining digital signatures and public-key cryptosystems|RSA78]] gives the scheme $\Enc(\pk, m) = m^e \bmod n$, $\Dec(\sk, c) = c^d \bmod n$, which is one-way but deterministic and hence not IND-CPA; IND-CPA security for single-bit messages follows by encrypting $b$ as $(x^e \bmod n,\; b \oplus h(x))$ for $x \getsr \ZZ_n^*$ and a hard-core predicate $h$ of the RSA function — [[ACGS88 - RSA and Rabin Functions Certain Parts are as Hard as the Whole|ACGS88]], [[GL89 - A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions|GL89]].
pages.sketch: The ciphertext $(x^e \bmod n,\, b \oplus h(x))$ hides $b$ exactly as well as $h(x)$ is unpredictable from $x^e \bmod n$, and decryption recovers $x = y^d \bmod n$ with the trapdoor $d$. An IND-CPA distinguisher is a predictor for $h$, which the hard-core reduction turns into an RSA inverter.
pages.improvements_text:
- The least-significant bit of the RSA function is hard-core: predicting it with advantage $1/\poly(\secpar)$ yields a full inverter — [[ACGS88 - RSA and Rabin Functions Certain Parts are as Hard as the Whole|ACGS88]].
- A hard-core predicate for every one-way function, giving the same bit encryption without an RSA-specific argument — [[GL89 - A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions|GL89]].
flags: rsa-to-pke-rsa78: RSA78's own scheme is deterministic and therefore not IND-CPA; the statement names the hard-core-bit step for that reason. If the wiki reads `pke` as syntax plus one-wayness only, RSA78 alone suffices and ACGS88/GL89 can be dropped.

rsa-to-pke-rsa78: this edge is the composite of red-rsa-to-tdp-rsa78 and red-tdp-to-pke. Direct assumption-to-PKE shortcuts are the repo norm (ddh-to-pke-elgamal85, lwe-to-pke-reg05, dcr-to-pke-pai99), so keeping it is consistent, but a human may prefer to delete it in favour of the two-link path.
rsa-to-pke-rsa78: ACGS88 needs a new reference page (verified: SIAM J. Comput. 17(2):194-209, 1988, DOI 10.1137/0217013).

sources.ref_file_title: RSA78 - A method for obtaining digital signatures and public-key cryptosystems
sources.authors: Ronald L. Rivest, Adi Shamir, Leonard Adleman

sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki; abstract read from content/References.

pages.class_justification: Left `unstated`. The hypothesis is a concrete hardness assumption, not a primitive quantified over implementations, so the RTV04 notions (which quantify over f in F_Q) are degenerate here; every other assumption-hypothesis edge in content/Reductions is likewise unstated, while all seven fully-black-box pages have primitive hypotheses. The security reduction is nonetheless black-box in the adversary. This edge is additionally degenerate: the 'construction' is the RSA family itself and the 'reduction' is the identity, so no class carries information.
pages.statement: The [[rsa-assumption|RSA assumption]] implies [[trapdoor-permutation|TDP]]: for $n = pq$ and $e$ coprime to $\varphi(n)$, the map $x \mapsto x^e \bmod n$ is a permutation of $\ZZ_n^*$ inverted by $y \mapsto y^d \bmod n$ with $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{\varphi(n)}$, and one-wayness of that family is the RSA assumption verbatim — [[RSA78 - A method for obtaining digital signatures and public-key cryptosystems|RSA78]]. The domain is $\ZZ_n^*$ rather than $\bits^\ell$, and applications that sample domain elements from their coins — oblivious transfer, NIZK — need the enhanced or doubly enhanced strengthenings of the notion — [[GR13 - Enhancements of Trapdoor Permutations|GR13]].
pages.improvements_text: - The enhanced and doubly enhanced variants of trapdoor permutations, which the oblivious-transfer and NIZK applications actually require, are defined, compared, and shown to suffice for those applications — [[GR13 - Enhancements of Trapdoor Permutations|GR13]].
flags: HIGH -- rsa-to-tdp-rsa78: the migrated Statement section carries two quotes that belong to other edges. The BFM88 bullet ('NIZK for all NP from trapdoor permutations ... in the CRS model') is the TDP + CRS => NIZK edge (model: crs), and the 'which in turn imply PKE' tail is red-tdp-to-pke. Both should be dropped from this page; the single trailing RSA78 citation is misattributed to them.

HIGH -- rsa-to-tdp-rsa78: the same misattributed bullet also produced content/Reductions/dlog-to-tdp.md ('DLOG => TDP', source: folklore), whose entire Statement is that BFM88 parenthetical. No trapdoor permutation is known from the discrete logarithm assumption; whoever owns that page's batch should dispose it wrong_claim.

rsa-to-tdp-rsa78: certifying that a claimed $(n, e)$ really indexes a permutation is a further caveat that GR13's enhancement axis does not cover. Left out of the statement rather than attached to a citation I did not verify.

pages.wrong_reason: The page body states 'Schnorr signatures implies Schnorr signatures' -- a self-loop -- while the frontmatter conclusion is `eddsa`, which names no object in the wiki: EdDSA/Ed25519 appears only as a bold parenthetical in content/Primitives/digital-signature.md line 152, with no page, no id, and no alias. The assertion the edge is trying to record, 'Schnorr signatures are the basis for EdDSA', is deployment lineage rather than a reduction: EdDSA IS Schnorr, instantiated over a twisted Edwards curve with deterministic nonce derivation and key prefixing, so there is no construction and no security reduction between two distinct objects. Everything reducible in the migrated Sch91 quote is already recorded elsewhere: red-dlog-and-rom-to-schnorr-signatures-sch91, red-dlog-to-schnorr-signatures-sch91 and red-fiat-shamir-and-schnorr-signatures-to-ds. The page should be deleted, not sourced.
flags: HIGH -- schnorr-signatures-to-schnorr-signatures: delete. Self-loop whose declared conclusion node `eddsa` does not exist anywhere in content/.

schnorr-signatures-to-schnorr-signatures: if the wiki ever wants an EdDSA object, the citable source for Ed25519 is Bernstein, Duif, Lange, Schwabe, Yang, 'High-Speed High-Security Signatures', CHES 2011 (journal version J. Cryptographic Engineering 2(2):77-89, 2012), verified at https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-23951-9_9. It belongs in a Variations subsection of digital-signature.md, not as a reduction edge.

schnorr-signatures-to-schnorr-signatures: the migrated quote's claim that Schnorr's sigma protocol 'is honest-verifier zero-knowledge under the discrete logarithm assumption' is wrong and lives on content/References/Sch91 - Efficient signature generation by smart cards.md, so it survives this page's deletion. The protocol is PERFECT HVZK unconditionally: the simulator samples $c, s$ and sets $R = g^s \pk^{-c}$.

sources.ref_file_title: Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography
sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki. The search-decision equivalence is Lemma 4.2 of the JACM version.

sources.ref_file_title: MM11b - Pseudorandom Knapsacks and the Sample Complexity of LWE Search-to-Decision Reductions
sources.note: Key MM11 is already taken in content/References by Matsuda-Matsuura, 'On Black-Box Separations among Injective One-Way Functions' (TCC 2011). Suffixed per the collision rule; a human may prefer to relabel both as MM11a/MM11b.

pages.class_justification: Left `unstated`. The hypothesis is a concrete hardness assumption, not a primitive quantified over implementations, so the RTV04 notions (which quantify over f in F_Q) are degenerate here; every other assumption-hypothesis edge in content/Reductions is likewise unstated, while all seven fully-black-box pages have primitive hypotheses. The security reduction is nonetheless black-box in the adversary.
pages.statement: If [[learning-with-errors#search-lwe|search LWE]] is hard for parameters $(n, q, \chi, m)$ with $q$ prime and $q = \poly(n)$, then [[learning-with-errors#decision-lwe|decision LWE]] is hard for the same parameters: any efficient distinguisher between $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{A}\mathbf{s} + \mathbf{e})$ and $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{u})$ is converted into an efficient algorithm that recovers $\mathbf{s}$ — [[Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography|Reg05]].
pages.sketch: Recover $\mathbf{s}$ one coordinate at a time. To test the guess $\mathbf{s}_i = \ell$, map each sample $(\mathbf{a}, b)$ to $(\mathbf{a} + r\mathbf{u}_i,\; b + r\ell)$ for a fresh uniform $r \in \ZZ_q$: the shifted sample is still LWE-distributed when $\ell = \mathbf{s}_i$ and uniform otherwise, since $r(\ell - \mathbf{s}_i)$ is uniform for prime $q$. Running the distinguisher over all $n \cdot q$ pairs $(i, \ell)$ reads off $\mathbf{s}$, which is why $q$ must be polynomially bounded; random self-reducibility first turns an average-case distinguisher into one that works for every $\mathbf{s}$.
pages.improvements_text: - Sample-preserving search-to-decision reductions: $m$ LWE samples are indistinguishable from uniform whenever search LWE is one-way for the same number $m$ of samples — [[MM11b - Pseudorandom Knapsacks and the Sample Complexity of LWE Search-to-Decision Reductions|MM11b]].
flags: HIGH -- search-lwe-to-decision-lwe: the migrated body proves the WRONG direction. Under the repo's orientation ('A => B' means 'A hard implies B hard', as fixed by cdh-to-dlog and ddh-to-cdh), this page is the hard direction -- a decision distinguisher yields a search solver, Reg05 Lemma 4.2 -- but the quoted text ('a search solver gives a decision adversary for free') proves red-decision-lwe-to-search-lwe. The two pages' Statement bodies are swapped: content/Reductions/decision-lwe-to-search-lwe.md currently carries the coordinate-by-coordinate Regev argument that belongs here. Fix both together.

search-lwe-to-decision-lwe: consequently the sibling red-decision-lwe-to-search-lwe is the EASY direction and is genuine folklore (run the search solver, accept iff $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{A}\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ is short), conditional on $\chi$ being efficiently recognisable. Its batch owner should not source it to Reg05, and its migration note about the $O(qnm)$ sample count belongs on this page instead.
search-lwe-to-decision-lwe: kept as `implication`, not `equivalence` -- both directions already exist as separate pages.

search-lwe-to-decision-lwe: proposed key MM11b because MM11 is already taken by Matsuda-Matsuura, 'On Black-Box Separations among Injective One-Way Functions'. A human may prefer MM11a/MM11b for both papers (the existing filename is a live URL and must not be renamed).

pages.wrong_reason: False under the wiki's own definitions. content/Primitives/single-server-private-information-retrieval.md line 97 defines SK-PIR as achieving $o(N)$ online communication 'without requiring sublinear server computation (contrast: SK-DEPIR, which requires both)', while content/Primitives/doubly-efficient-pir.md requires BOTH communication and query-time computation to be $o(n)$. Adding SKE lets the client outsource its state to the server, but it cannot turn linear server work into sublinear server work: BM26's SK-PIR from one-way functions has $O(N \cdot \poly(\secpar))$ server time per query, and it still does after the state is encrypted. The quoted text is also not a theorem of any paper -- it is an editor's aside in the Notes of content/References/CIMR25 - Secret-Key PIR from Random Linear Codes.md ('But I could preprecess the database and store the state encrypted on the server'), specific to CIMR25's own $O(s + n/s)$ construction, and downloading the encrypted state on every query puts per-query communication at $|\st|$ unless the cost is amortised, which the text does not say.
flags: HIGH -- secret-key-pir-sk-pir-and-ske-to-depir: delete the page, or keep the idea as a note on the CIMR25 reference page. It is an unattributed editor construction and false as a general implication between the wiki's SK-PIR and DEPIR nodes.

secret-key-pir-sk-pir-and-ske-to-depir: supporting evidence already in the wiki -- content/Primitives/doubly-efficient-pir.md cites LMW25 ('Black Box Crypto is Useless for Doubly Efficient PIR') for the claim that generic primitives cannot give SK-DEPIR in a black-box way unless OWFs already do.

pages.wrong_reason: Same definitional obstruction as red-secret-key-pir-sk-pir-and-ske-to-depir: the wiki defines SK-PIR as giving $o(N)$ online communication WITHOUT sublinear server computation, which is exactly the extra requirement DEPIR imposes, so SK-PIR alone cannot imply DEPIR. BIPW17 assert no such implication: they build SK-DEPIR (an oblivious locally decodable code) from a specific permuted-puzzles / permuted Reed-Muller hardness conjecture, which the wiki already records as red-permuted-puzzles-to-depir-bipw17. The migrated sentence is the editor's inference by analogy ('the way that BIPW17 build SK-DEPIR') from a Notes section of the CIMR25 reference page, and its qualifier 'very mildly doubly efficient PIR' names no notion defined anywhere in content/, so the conclusion node is untypable as written.
flags: HIGH -- secret-key-pir-sk-pir-to-depir-bipw17: delete. The real BIPW17 edge is already in the graph as red-permuted-puzzles-to-depir-bipw17; this page duplicates its citation while stating an implication BIPW17 does not prove.
secret-key-pir-sk-pir-to-depir-bipw17: the frontmatter cites BIPW17 for a claim taken from CIMR25's Notes; the source field is misattributed even before the mathematical problem.

sources.ref_file_title: JDF11 - Towards quantum-resistant cryptosystems from supersingular elliptic curve isogenies
sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki. Verified that JDF11 prove session-key security in the authenticated-links model under SSDDH, the decisional variant.

pages.class_justification: Left `unstated`. The hypothesis is a concrete hardness assumption, not a primitive quantified over implementations, so the RTV04 notions (which quantify over f in F_Q) are degenerate here; every other assumption-hypothesis edge in content/Reductions is likewise unstated, while all seven fully-black-box pages have primitive hypotheses. The security reduction is nonetheless black-box in the adversary. The key-exchange security proof here is essentially the identity: session-key indistinguishability is SSDDH restated for the protocol transcript.
pages.model_justification: JDF11 prove session-key security in the Canetti-Krawczyk authenticated-links adversarial model under SSDDH, with no idealized oracle; `standard` is the correct value.
pages.statement: The [[supersingular-isogeny-diffie-hellman|SIDH]] assumption implies [[key-exchange|KE]]: in the Jao-De Feo protocol each party walks a secret isogeny from a fixed supersingular $E/\FF_{p^2}$ with $p + 1 = \ell_A^{e_A}\ell_B^{e_B}$, publishes its image curve together with the images of a basis of the other party's torsion subgroup, and both derive the shared key $j(E_{AB})$; the session key is indistinguishable from uniform in the authenticated-links model under the decisional variant SSDDH — [[JDF11 - Towards quantum-resistant cryptosystems from supersingular elliptic curve isogenies|JDF11]]. The hypothesis is now known to be false: the published torsion-point images make the secret isogeny recoverable in classical polynomial time — [[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]].
pages.sketch: Each party's secret is an isogeny with kernel $\langle P + [s]Q \rangle$ for a basis $\{P, Q\}$ of its own torsion subgroup. Publishing the images of the OTHER party's basis points lets each side push its own kernel forward onto the received curve, so both compute the same image curve up to isomorphism and agree on its $j$-invariant; distinguishing that $j$-invariant from a random one is SSDDH by definition.
notes_to_keep: SUSPECTED ERROR on content/Assumptions/supersingular-isogeny-diffie-hellman.md: the shared-key line $j(E_{AB}) = j(\phi_B(E_A)) = j(\phi_A(E_B))$ applies each party's own isogeny to the other party's curve. The correct objects are the pushed-forward isogenies $\phi_B' : E_A \to E_{AB}$ and $\phi_A' : E_B \to E_{AB}$ computed from the transmitted torsion-point images; as written the composition is not defined.

SUSPECTED ERROR on the same page: the SIDH problem is stated with $E' = E/\langle P \rangle$ for a random $\ell$-torsion point $P$ while $\{P, Q\}$ is called a basis of the $\ell^n$-torsion. The kernel is $\langle P + [s]Q \rangle$ for a secret $s$, and both basis images of the other party's torsion group are published.
flags: sidh-to-ke-jdf11: .reductions/suspected-errors.json contains an entry whose affectsEdges lists red-sidh-to-ke-jdf11. Both suspected errors are about the assumption page's description of the protocol, not about this edge's claim; the edge itself is sound and stays `sourced`. Kept verbatim in notes_to_keep.

sidh-to-ke-jdf11: the wiki's KE security notion is session-key indistinguishability, which needs the DECISIONAL assumption (SSDDH). content/Assumptions/supersingular-isogeny-diffie-hellman.md states only the computational isogeny-finding problem and has no pseudocode game at all, so the hypothesis node is weaker than what the reduction uses.
sidh-to-ke-jdf11: the reduction remains valid while its hypothesis is false (CD22). The statement says so; CD22 already has a reference page, so no new reference is needed.

pages.class_justification: The construction is the identity -- an SPIR scheme run unchanged is a cPIR scheme -- so it uses the hypothesis scheme only as an oracle, and a client-privacy adversary against the resulting cPIR is verbatim a client-privacy adversary against the SPIR, so the single fixed reduction uses it as an oracle. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape in its trivial case.
pages.statement: Single-server [[single-server-private-information-retrieval#symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server|symmetric PIR]] implies [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|cPIR]]: SPIR is cPIR plus the requirement that the client learn nothing about $D$ beyond the single entry it retrieves, and it weakens nothing on the client-privacy side, so every SPIR scheme is a cPIR scheme unchanged — folklore. Data privacy for PIR is due to [[GIKM00 - Protecting Data Privacy in Private Information Retrieval Scheme|GIKM00]].
flags: symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-cpir: kept `folklore` -- a strengthened notion implying the weaker one is definitional, and GIKM00 is cited in the statement for the origin of data privacy, not for the containment. GIKM00 already has a reference page, so sources[] is deliberately empty.

symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-cpir: hypothesis and conclusion live in the same file (single-server-symmetric-pir is an anchor on content/Primitives/single-server-private-information-retrieval.md). Same shape as red-unkeyed-depir-to-depir and red-spir-to-it-pir, so acceptable if the wiki keeps variant-to-parent edges.

sources.ref_file_title: NP99 - Oblivious transfer and polynomial evaluation
sources.note: Verified via ACM DL and Semantic Scholar: gives 1-out-of-N OT from log N invocations of 1-out-of-2 OT, and as a direct corollary an efficient transformation of any PIR into SPIR without adding servers.

sources.ref_file_title: DMO00 - Single Database Private Information Retrieval Implies Oblivious Transfer
sources.authors: Giovanni Di Crescenzo, Tal Malkin, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki (also used by red-cpir-to-ot-dmo00).

pages.class_justification: For the direction that holds, the construction is the identity: the SPIR protocol run on database $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ with query index $c$ IS 1-out-of-n OT, client privacy being receiver privacy and data privacy sender privacy. Both security reductions run the OT adversary as an oracle against the corresponding SPIR property.
pages.statement: Single-server [[single-server-private-information-retrieval#symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server|symmetric PIR]] implies [[oblivious-transfer|OT]]: an SPIR protocol run on the database $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ with query index $c$ is exactly [[oblivious-transfer#k-out-of-n-ot|$1$-out-of-$n$ OT]] — client privacy is receiver privacy, data privacy is sender privacy — and taking $n = 2$ gives $1$-out-of-$2$ OT — folklore. The converse fails as stated: SPIR is $1$-out-of-$n$ OT with communication sublinear in $n$, and OT on its own yields only the trivial $\Omega(n)$-communication protocol.
pages.improvements_text:
- Any single-server [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|PIR]] is upgraded to SPIR using $\log n$ invocations of $1$-out-of-$2$ OT, which is the converse direction under its missing efficiency hypothesis — [[NP99 - Oblivious transfer and polynomial evaluation|NP99]].
- Non-trivial single-server PIR already implies OT, without any data-privacy requirement — [[DMO00 - Single Database Private Information Retrieval Implies Oblivious Transfer|DMO00]].
flags: HIGH -- symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-ot: `kind` must change from equivalence to implication. The page's own qualifier ('with an additional efficiency requirement') is what breaks the equivalence: SPIR => 1-out-of-n OT is immediate, but OT => SPIR is false without a sublinear-communication PIR (NP99 needs a PIR plus log n OTs, and DMO00 shows the PIR hypothesis is the load-bearing one).

HIGH -- symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-ot: content/Reductions/k-out-of-n-ot-to-cpir.md ('1-out-of-n OT <=> cPIR', kind: equivalence, source: folklore) is the same claim pointed the other way and is false in ITS stated direction -- 1-out-of-n OT with Omega(n) communication is trivial from any OT and gives only trivial PIR. Whoever owns that batch should downgrade or invert it; the two pages must end up consistent.

symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-ot: NP99 needs a new reference page (verified: STOC 1999, pp. 245-254, DOI 10.1145/301250.301312; the PIR-to-SPIR transformation is a stated corollary of its 1-out-of-N OT protocol).
symmetric-private-information-retrieval-single-server-to-ot: the migrated body's `[[OT]]` bare-alias wikilink should become `[[oblivious-transfer|OT]]`.

sources.ref_file_title: GPV08 - Trapdoors for hard lattices and new cryptographic constructions
sources.authors: Craig Gentry, Chris Peikert, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
sources.note: Already a reference page in the wiki.

Verified via Springer and the IACR archive PDF. Springer renders the title 'Lattice Signatures without Trapdoors'; eprint 2011/537 capitalises 'Without'. Contribution used here: a scheme based on plain SIS (not only ring-SIS), in the ROM, with no trapdoor.

sources.ref_file_title: CHKP10 - Bonsai Trees, or How to Delegate a Lattice Basis
sources.authors: David Cash, Dennis Hofheinz, Eike Kiltz, Chris Peikert
sources.note: Verified via DBLP and Springer: gives an efficient stateless hash-and-sign signature in the standard model (no random oracles) and the first pairing-free HIBE.

pages.class_justification: Left `unstated`. The hypothesis is a concrete hardness assumption, not a primitive quantified over implementations, so the RTV04 notions (which quantify over f in F_Q) are degenerate here; every other assumption-hypothesis edge in content/Reductions is likewise unstated, while all seven fully-black-box pages have primitive hypotheses. The security reduction is nonetheless black-box in the adversary.
pages.model_justification: GPV hash-and-sign is proved EUF-CMA in the random oracle model -- the reduction programs $H$ by sampling the preimage first -- so the current frontmatter value `standard` is wrong. A standard-model SIS signature does exist (CHKP10), which would support a separate model: standard edge rather than a change to this one.
pages.statement: The [[shortest-integer-solution|SIS]] assumption implies [[digital-signature|DS]] in the random oracle model: a GPV signature on $\mu$ is a short vector $\mathbf{z}$ with $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{z} = H(\mu) \bmod q$, produced by discrete Gaussian preimage sampling with a trapdoor for $\mathbf{A}$, and a forgery is a short solution to the inhomogeneous problem ISIS, which is polynomially equivalent to SIS under mild parameter conditions — [[GPV08 - Trapdoors for hard lattices and new cryptographic constructions|GPV08]].
pages.sketch: The signing key is a short basis of $\Lambda_q^\perp(\mathbf{A})$ and signatures are discrete Gaussian preimages of $H(\mu)$, whose distribution does not depend on which trapdoor produced them; the reduction can therefore answer signing queries by sampling $\mathbf{z}$ first and programming $H(\mu) := \mathbf{A}\mathbf{z}$ on a challenge $\mathbf{A}$ it did not generate. A forgery on an unqueried message is then a short ISIS solution for that $\mathbf{A}$.
pages.improvements_text:
- Signatures whose security reduces to plain SIS with no lattice trapdoor, via Fiat-Shamir with aborts and rejection sampling; the line of work behind Dilithium — [[Lyu12 - Lattice Signatures Without Trapdoors|Lyu12]].
- Stateless hash-and-sign signatures from SIS in the standard model, removing the random oracle, via bonsai-tree basis delegation — [[CHKP10 - Bonsai Trees, or How to Delegate a Lattice Basis|CHKP10]].
flags: HIGH -- sis-to-ds: `model` must change from standard to rom for the GPV08 claim.

sis-to-ds: near-duplicate of content/Reductions/isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-ds-gpv08.md, which carries the same GPV08 hash-and-sign claim with hypothesis inhomogeneous-sis (and the wiki also has isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis). Either merge the two, or keep this page as the trapdoor-free Lyu12 edge / the standard-model CHKP10 edge and leave GPV08 on the ISIS page. A third, older route also exists in the graph: sis-to-hash-function-ajt96 followed by hash-function-to-ds.

sis-to-ds: the migrated bullet on content/Primitives/digital-signature.md is tagged '-- standard' although GPV08 is its canonical citation and already has a reference page; that folklore flag should be replaced by the citation (CLAUDE.md: 'obvious to a working cryptographer' is not folklore).
sis-to-ds: Lyu12 and CHKP10 need new reference pages.
